issues.description: Class attributes visibility differs between the template and the specification/solution. The template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) declares two fields as public (lectureName and numberOfInscribedStudents at lines 4-5), while the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) shows all Lecture attributes as private (-lectureName, -numberOfInscribedStudents, -numberOfGuestStudents, -numberOfLecturers, -numberOfTutors at lines 63-68) and the solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) implements all five attributes as private (lines 6-10). This mismatch can confuse students about the intended encapsulation and whether to implement private fields with getters/setters or to keep public fields.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template consistent with the UML and the reference solution. Change the existing public fields in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to private (lectureName and numberOfInscribedStudents) and declare the remaining attributes (private int numberOfGuestStudents, private int numberOfLecturers, private int numberOfTutors) as private as well. Keep the constructor/getter/setter/toString TODOs in the template so students still implement behavior, but ensure the attribute visibility matches the specification to avoid confusion about encapsulation.
